purpose: Determine whether the user's RX 7800 XT workstation can reliably train, save and reload a small QLoRA adapter outside the RIC runtime before any real RIC training dataset is created.
non_goals: Do not measure whether LoRA improves RIC behavior.
Do not tune the final RIC adapter.
Do not modify the RIC runtime, DB, provider contracts or product dependencies.
Do not use V3c artifacts, character data, memories or production prompts.
Do not treat hotswap support as mandatory for basic training feasibility.
preferred_first_environment: WSL2 plus a ROCm/PyTorch combination that explicitly supports RX 7800 XT gfx1101 at execution time; verify current compatibility before installation rather than relying on this draft's date.
environment_identity_required: GPU exact model and reported gfx target
PyTorch version and ROCm/HIP build identity
TRL or selected SFT trainer version if used
bitsandbytes version and backend identity if used
exact base-model artifact and revision used for the smoke test
isolation_rules: Use an environment separate from the RIC product environment unless Codex later decides otherwise.
No package changes to RIC pyproject.toml or its runtime environment in this experiment.
Use a synthetic micro-dataset containing no RIC names, lore, prompts or benchmark cases.
Write outputs to a dedicated experiment directory, never the V3c worktree or DB directory.
Record failures as evidence; do not silently switch backend, quantization or model artifact without starting a new attempt record.

ordered_checks.pass_condition: PyTorch sees the intended AMD GPU through the selected ROCm/HIP stack and reports a usable accelerator device without falling back to CPU.
Representative tensor operations on the GPU complete without backend error, NaN/Inf anomaly attributable to the stack, or device reset.
The exact smoke-test base model loads in the intended low-bit configuration on GPU with measured VRAM/RAM and can perform a forward/generation pass.
A fresh LoRA adapter can be attached while the base weights remain frozen; trainable-parameter accounting is recorded and materially smaller than the base parameter count.

A bounded synthetic SFT run completes multiple optimizer steps without OOM, backend crash, device reset, persistent NaN loss or unintended base-weight training. Exact step count is fixed in the execution WO before the attempt.
Adapter configuration and weights save successfully, a fresh process can load the same base artifact plus saved adapter, and inference completes.
The experiment can identify and run the base-only condition separately from base-plus-adapter without requiring a permanently merged model artifact. Exact mechanism is backend-dependent.

On a synthetic training example or designated development probe, the reloaded adapter produces a measurable trained effect relative to the same frozen base under controlled decoding. This is only a pipeline sanity check, not RIC-quality evidence.

If the selected inference stack exposes compatible LoRA hotswap, replace or disable an adapter without reloading the base and verify effective adapter identity. Failure here does not make QLoRA training infeasible.

Repeat the bounded train/save/reload path in a fresh process or second attempt without an unexplained one-off success. Identical floating-point results are not required across nondeterministic kernels; operational success must repeat.

measurements_per_check: whether CPU offload occurred and where

verdicts.FEASIBLE: All required checks pass on a repeatable stack without a workaround that makes maintenance clearly unreasonable; limitations are documented but do not prevent the intended small QLoRA experiment.
verdicts.FEASIBLE_WITH_LIMITS: All core training/save/reload checks pass, but material constraints such as sequence-length pressure, CPU offload, fragile package pinning, unsupported optional hotswap or significant performance limits must shape the later training design.
verdicts.NOT_YET_FEASIBLE: A required core check cannot be made reliable on the tested supported stack, such as quantized load, backward/optimizer steps, save/reload or repeatability. Record the blocker; do not patch RIC to compensate.

anti_overinterpretation: A successful micro-run proves technical pipeline feasibility only; it does not prove that the desired sequence length, dataset size or training time is practical.
A low training loss on the synthetic micro-dataset is not evidence that RIC discipline was learned.
Same seed does not guarantee byte-identical training across changed kernels, libraries or hardware execution paths.
Optional hotswap failure does not invalidate non-merged adapter loading.
A single lucky run is not enough; repeatability is a required check.
next_gate_if_feasible: Freeze the behavioral benchmark design, then create a separate RIC training-data plan. Do not train the real adapter directly from this smoke test.
